summary: Core protocol (swarm_init once, concurrent wave spawn, 5xx-only retry, 409 single-retry, module separation) is correctly implemented. Five blocking defects: asyncio.gather silently drops all-but-first simultaneous exceptions; _spawn_one bypasses the workspace_client.lease() context manager and deletes the worktree on the success path (agent runs in deleted cwd); _with_retry lacks a type annotation on request_fn; deps are lower-bound-only with no lockfile; zero direct unit tests cover WorkspaceClient._with_retry, workspace_client.lease, or any ruflo_client logic.

checks.title: asyncio.gather usage — return_exceptions missing
checks.detail: _dispatch_wave calls asyncio.gather(*[self._spawn_one(...)]) with no return_exceptions=True. Under Python asyncio semantics, when one coroutine raises, gather propagates that exception but does NOT cancel siblings — they continue running. However if gather itself is cancelled (e.g. by an outer timeout or KeyboardInterrupt) all siblings receive CancelledError, which is a BaseException, not caught by the bare 'except Exception' in _spawn_one. This means the finally: await self._safe_delete() block can be bypassed for cancelled siblings, leaking worktrees. Additionally, when multiple tasks fail simultaneously gather returns only the first exception; the rest are silently discarded, violating the requirement that errors surface to the originating topic (D12 / docstring line 20). The test test_partial_failure_does_not_leak_worktrees passes because mock callables have no async yield points where CancelledError could interrupt the finally.
checks.recommendation: Use asyncio.gather(*coroutines, return_exceptions=True). After awaiting, iterate results: collect all exceptions, re-raise as ExceptionGroup (Python 3.11+) or raise the first after logging the rest. This guarantees each coroutine reaches its finally block under cancellation and all errors are reported.

checks.title: Context manager for worktree lifetime — lease() bypassed
checks.detail: The task spec hint (tasks/14.md line 65) and workspace_client.py:156-182 both define and document the workspace.lease() asynccontextmanager as the canonical lifetime abstraction. SwarmBridge._spawn_one does NOT use it: it calls _lease_worktree_with_capacity_retry() directly, then manages cleanup manually in a try/finally. Consequently: (a) the workspace_client.lease() context manager is dead code never exercised by the bridge; (b) the manual path duplicates delete logic already present in lease(). More critically, _spawn_one calls _safe_delete in the finally block, meaning the worktree is deleted on the SUCCESS path immediately after spawn_agent() returns — before the spawned agent finishes using its cwd on disk. If workspace_client DELETE removes the git worktree from the filesystem (the normal expectation), the running agent is left with a non-existent working directory. This defect is masked by tests because spawn_agent is mocked as instantaneous.
checks.recommendation: Refactor _spawn_one to use 'async with self._workspace.lease(...) as cwd:' and move the spawn_agent call inside the block. The worktree lifetime should span the full duration of agent execution, not just the spawn_agent MCP handshake. Extend workspace_client.lease() to accept an optional capacity_wait_s parameter if the retry behaviour is needed, rather than re-implementing it in swarm_bridge.

checks.title: finally block reliability — _safe_delete on success path
checks.detail: Related to CHK-CR-2 but distinct: regardless of whether lease() is used, the current _spawn_one finally block runs unconditionally on both success and failure paths. This is architecturally wrong for the success case: an agent has been dispatched with a cwd that will immediately cease to exist on disk. On the failure path (spawn_agent raises), deleting the worktree is correct. The semantic contract should be: delete on error, preserve on success (until the agent completes). Using the context manager correctly (wrapping both spawn and agent lifetime) resolves this. As a minimal fix short of the context manager refactor: move _safe_delete out of finally into the except block only, and track worktree paths for deferred cleanup by the caller.
checks.evidence: swarm_bridge.py:233-234 — finally always fires after spawn_agent returns
checks.recommendation: Move cleanup to except path only until the full lease() refactor is in place. Add a comment flagging that agent completion signals (ruflo callbacks or polling) should trigger deferred cleanup.

checks.title: Pydantic v2 model correctness
checks.detail: All six Pydantic models (SwarmConfig, AgentConfig, SwarmHandle, AgentHandle, WorktreeCreated, WorktreeDeleted) use BaseModel with no class Config inner class (correct v2 style; v1 used class Config). Field() calls use the ge= constraint syntax (not v1's gt/ge in a validator decorator). model_validate() is used instead of parse_obj(). No root_validator or @validator decorators. The type annotations are standard Python 3.10+ union syntax (str | None). One minor observation: AgentConfig.cwd has no path existence validator — a non-absolute or non-existent path would pass model validation silently. This is acceptable at the model layer (validation responsibility belongs to the workspace-manager) but worth a comment.
checks.recommendation: Add Field(..., description='Absolute filesystem path') to AgentConfig.cwd and WorktreeCreated.path to document the contract. Optionally add a field_validator checking path.startswith('/') for local safety.

checks.title: httpx retry strategy — 5xx only, not 4xx
checks.detail: workspace_client._with_retry checks response.status_code < 500 and returns immediately for any non-5xx response (including 4xx and 2xx/3xx). Only responses with status_code >= 500 are retried. _raise_for_status then converts 409 to CapacityError, other 4xx to WorkspaceClientError, and calls response.raise_for_status() for persistent 5xx after retries exhausted. The boundary is correct. One edge case: HTTP 5xx responses carry no explicit check for status_code == 599 (network-level synthetic codes from httpx proxies) — these would also be retried, which is acceptable. Note: network-level exceptions (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException) are NOT caught by _with_retry since it only inspects response objects; a connection failure would propagate immediately without retry.
checks.recommendation: Document the no-retry-on-network-error behaviour in the method docstring. Consider catching httpx.TransportError in _with_retry for production robustness, though this is a separate concern from the 4xx/5xx boundary.

checks.title: Type hints completeness
checks.detail: WorkspaceClient._with_retry(self, request_fn) has no type annotation for the request_fn parameter. The correct annotation is Callable[[], Awaitable[httpx.Response]] or equivalently Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, httpx.Response]]. Without it, mypy treats the parameter as Any and provides no type-checking for callers passing wrong callables. All other public methods in all three modules have complete return type annotations. RufloClient correctly defines McpCallable = Callable[..., Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]] for its injectable callables (ruflo_client.py:41). The _with_retry gap is inconsistent with this pattern.
checks.recommendation: Add annotation: 'async def _with_retry(self, request_fn: Callable[[], Awaitable[httpx.Response]]) -> httpx.Response'. Import Callable and Awaitable from collections.abc (preferred over typing in Python 3.12+, though typing aliases still work).

checks.title: Test quality — edge case coverage
checks.detail: 15/15 tests pass but coverage has material gaps: (a) No test for WorkspaceClient._with_retry exhausting all 3 retries on consecutive 5xx and surfacing httpx.HTTPStatusError — only the 409/CapacityError path is exercised through bridge mocks. (b) No test for workspace_client.lease() context manager directly (it is never used by swarm_bridge, so it has zero test coverage). (c) No test for swarm_init() failure propagation — if ruflo.init_swarm() raises, no worktrees have been created yet but the test suite has no case asserting dispatch() re-raises cleanly. (d) No test for an empty waves list (FeaturePlan(waves=[])) — dispatch would call swarm_init with task_count=0, violating SwarmConfig.task_count ge=1 and raising a Pydantic ValidationError, which is untested. (e) test_concurrent_features_dont_collide contains dead code at lines 395-396 (ruflo_a and ruflo_b are constructed but immediately overwritten at lines 405-406); this is a code quality defect in the test itself. (f) No direct unit tests for ruflo_client.py — RufloClient.init_swarm and RufloClient.spawn_agent are only exercised indirectly through bridge fixtures.
checks.evidence: tests/test_swarm_bridge.py:395-396 (dead ruflo_a/b); pyproject.toml line 9 (requires-python = >=3.12); SwarmConfig ge=1 with no empty-waves test
checks.recommendation: Add: test_with_retry_exhausts_5xx_and_raises (httpx mock returning 500 three times), test_swarm_init_failure_propagates (swarm_init_fn raises, assert dispatch raises, no DELETE called), test_dispatch_empty_waves_raises_validation_error, unit tests for RufloClient directly. Remove dead ruflo_a/b lines 395-396 in test_concurrent_features_dont_collide.

checks.title: pyproject.toml dependencies — pinning strategy
checks.detail: Runtime deps use lower-bound-only ranges: httpx>=0.27.0 and pydantic>=2.7.0. Dev deps: pytest>=8.2.0, pytest-asyncio>=1.0.0, pytest-cov>=5.0.0. There is no upper bound and no lockfile (uv.lock, requirements.txt, or pip-tools .txt). This means: (a) httpx 1.0 (breaking API changes expected when released) would be silently picked up in CI; (b) pydantic 3.x (if released) could break model_validate semantics; (c) CI reproducibility is not guaranteed — different install times get different transitive dependency versions. The requires-python = >=3.12 is correct (uses 3.10+ union syntax and relies on 3.12 asyncio behaviour).
checks.evidence: pyproject.toml:13-23; no uv.lock or requirements*.txt in fabric/integrations/
checks.recommendation: Add upper-bound pins: httpx>=0.27.0,<1.0; pydantic>=2.7.0,<3.0. Generate a lockfile (uv lock or pip-compile) and commit it. Alternatively add a compatible-release specifier: httpx~=0.27, pydantic~=2.7.

checks.title: Module separation — swarm_bridge / workspace_client / ruflo_client
checks.detail: The three concerns are correctly separated into three distinct modules with clean one-directional import topology: swarm_bridge imports from workspace_client and ruflo_client; workspace_client and ruflo_client do not import from each other or from swarm_bridge. Domain models (TaskSpec, FeaturePlan, DispatchResult) live in swarm_bridge; HTTP response shapes (WorktreeCreated, WorktreeDeleted, CapacityError, WorkspaceClientError) in workspace_client; MCP callable shapes (SwarmConfig, AgentConfig, SwarmHandle, AgentHandle) in ruflo_client. The RufloClient injectable-callable pattern keeps ruflo_client free of MCP SDK imports, making it independently testable. The McpCallable type alias is exported from ruflo_client for use by callers wiring the real MCP tools.
checks.evidence: fabric/integrations/__init__.py; import sections of all three .py files
checks.recommendation: None. Module boundaries and separation of concerns are clean.
